The key takeaways are: • The experimental unit capacity for Case #1 (AHRI 210/240 H1 Test) is the same Full as the rated capacity (4-Ton, 14.1 kW). This proves that the HP-TES unit running without TES does not experience degraded performance. • For Case #6 (AHRI 210/240 H3 Test), the overall heating capacity is lower, Full which is expected due to the lower ambient temperature. Nevertheless, the same conclusion can be drawn: baseline HP operation (no TES used) remains unchanged even when the unit is connected to the TES loop. The HP-TES model predicts the overall system performance (heat load, compressor power) and compressor temperatures (suction, discharge) very well. • The system start-up deviations can be attributed to the reported experimental data being measured at steady-state, while the Modelica model assumes system start- up. However, the steady-state model performance matches very well, thus validating the model predictions. • Heat load deviations during steady-state operation are attributed to cabinet heat losses, which are especially pronounced in Case #6, which has a low ambient temperature (Ambient DBT/WBT = 17°F/15°F). The previously done (ORNL & EPRI tests) baseline unit only testing o indicated that the heat loss was around ~15%. When applying this value to the Modelica-predicted heat load, the agreement was significantly better.
